answer.summary: No verifiable evidence of memory retention mechanisms under stable, low-variation input conditions exists in the available sources, and the claimed baseline persistence remains unanchored and unsupported.
answer.content: After two review cycles, no source provides explicit descriptions of memory retention mechanisms or the longest observed duration without state decay under stable input. While S2 outlines a layered memory lifecycle and S1 raises privacy concerns, neither addresses persistence duration under low-variation conditions. The absence of temporally structured, verifiable data prevents any claim of superiority in memory management. A bounded revision is required to clarify what constitutes sufficient evidence before further evaluation can proceed.
answer.search: find Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 full text or abstract with explicit descriptions of memory retention mechanisms under stable, low-variation input conditions and any reported duration of state persistence

answer.lesson: All claims about agent memory persistence must be grounded in explicit, verifiable source descriptions under defined conditions; absence of such data necessitates a bounded revision to clarify evidence requirements before any evaluation can proceed, regardless of theoretical plausibility or system design claims.'
